item.title: Ticket shock as FIFA World Cup resale market drives prices sky high
item.description: Ticket prices for 2026 World Cup skyrocketed on FIFA's official resale platform, with seats for final reaching an eye-watering $143,750.

item.title: Tragedy on Nile as ferry sinks, leaving 15 dead in Sudan
item.description: Passenger ferry carrying more than 27 people, including women and children, capsizes in Nile River between Taiba Al-Khawad and Deim Al-Qarray.

item.title: Bangladesh's dual vote: Why a referendum is being held with the general election
item.description: More than 127.6 million people are eligible to vote, with polling stations open from 7:30 am (0130 GMT) to 4:30 pm (1030 GMT).

item.title: Fresh protests in Melbourne as Herzog wraps up Australia visit
item.description: Demonstrators rally on the final day of the Israeli president’s trip, capping a week of nationwide protests and clashes that have exposed deep divisions over Gaza.

item.title: Village evacuated after debris from missile attack hits Russian military site: official
item.description: Russian authorities say air defences repelled a strike in the Volgograd region, but falling fragments set a defence ministry facility ablaze near Kotluban.

item.title: US, Mexico seize cocaine in rare coordinated Pacific operation
item.description: Multiple people have been arrested, the Mexican navy says, without specifying how many.

item.title: Brazil orders X to block Grok's sexualised deepfakes immediately
item.description: Regulators give Elon Musk’s platform five days to stop its AI chatbot from generating explicit deepfake images of women and children or face fines and legal action.

item.title: After the revolution, Bangladesh's youth face democracy’s hardest test
item.description: After toppling Sheikh Hasina’s government in a historic uprising, a generation of young voters must now prove it can build institutions, not just dismantle regimes.

item.title: US, Iran showing flexibility on nuclear deal: Türkiye's Fidan
item.description: In an interview with the Financial Times, Fidan signals cautious optimism over revived US–Iran talks while urging both sides to focus strictly on the nuclear file and avoid “another war in the region.”

item.title: Post-uprising polls mark end of 'nightmare': Bangladesh's Yunus
item.description: People head to the polls for Bangladesh’s first election since the 2024 uprising that ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina.
